title: Simultaneous primitive roots: a conditional lower bound for prime bases
main_claim: Assume Inputs 1–4, imported from the companion paper "Primitive roots for every admissible integer base": a uniform Hecke zero-free half-plane for cyclotomic fields, a marked Type II estimate, a block sieve and a rough-number density. Then for any fixed distinct primes q_1..q_k, at least c x/(log x)^2 primes p in (x,2x) have every q_i as a primitive root.

issues.description: The theorem is conditional on a statement at least as strong as quasi-RH for the Riemann zeta function. The paper calls these inputs hypotheses and says so openly, so this is not a logical gap. But the word 'conditional' hides how strong the assumption is: one of the inputs is an open problem of quasi-RH strength.
issues.evidence: Input 1 says that for every cyclotomic F containing mu_12 and every finite-order Hecke character, L_F(s,chi) has no zeros in Re s>1-1e-6. Take F=Q(mu_12) and the trivial character. Then zeta_F = zeta(s) times entire Dirichlet L-functions, so zeta(s) would have no zeros in Re s>1-1e-6. The sibling review of the companion paper (rank 100) says that paper's proof of this rests on a new theta-reflection moment that it could only check for internal consistency.

coverage: I read all sections in full and checked them against the four Inputs. Section 2 (reduction): p=4rQ+1 with r,Q odd gives p≡5 mod 8, so (2/p)=-1. Reciprocity with p≡a (a nonresidue mod q_i) gives (q_i/p)=-1, so each index is odd. The case Q | index gives j<2x^0.1 and is bounded through log of prod(q^j-1) ≪ x^0.2. The case ℓ | r is handled by summing over ℓ, and both ratios to x/L^2 tend to 0. Group primes, with a_i in (0.1,0.2), fall inside (exp L^0.1, exp L^0.3). Section 3: I checked the Kummer degree ℓ(ℓ-1) via the Eisenstein argument, the discriminant bound ℓ^{ℓ(2ℓ-3)}q^{(ℓ-1)^2}, and the Frobenius/complete-splitting identification. The transfer to zeta_K through K~=F_ℓ(q^{1/ℓ}) with abelian Artin formalism is valid, since the denominator L-functions are entire. In the smooth explicit formula, the residue at 0 is -(r1+r2-1)Φ(0) ≤ 0. The unit-height zero count and the final bound x/(ℓ(ℓ-1)L)+x^{1-η} also check out. Section 4: the mark bound, J_0≥1, the Euler-product/Rankin tail and the PNT in a progression mod M hold. The Bombieri–Vinogradov exponent margin is (κ-ε)(1+ε)/4, which I recomputed. Lemma 4.3 checks, and so does the twisting by χ_0 to modulus lcm(M,k) ≤ L^{A_0+1}. The sieve-product identity giving 𝔖_M checks, including the factors at p | M. Section 5: initial sieve level b(4H_b+2) ≤ 1/5+2b < 1/2-κ/2. In the conditioned bin count, the moduli nℓ are injective and stay below D_0. In the Type II application, the exponent window [1/2+κ/2, 1-b/2] contains every m-dyad, γ < w_-, the Fourier separation and character expansion are valid, and the per-box error times O(L) boxes is o(X_0/L). The Buchstab bin decomposition and the partition step check (I verified the least-factor combinatorics). In the balanced-semiprime sieve, the bad residue count is 3j-2, and the identity 1-g(j)=(1-1/j)^3(1-1/(j-1)^2) checks algebraically. The lattice remainder sums are x^0.58 and x^0.17 against x/r with r ≤ x^0.11, and C_2 does not depend on κ, b or K. The parameter order κ→ε→b→partition→K→a_i→x is consistent, and the final 1-3/8 > 1/2 checks. I did not check the Inputs themselves; they are hypotheses taken from the companion paper.
sibling_notes: The companion paper "Primitive roots for every admissible integer base" (fam 029, rank 100) also came back no_gap_found, but it rests on the new uniform Hecke zero-free strip. This paper imports exactly that strip as Input 1, plus companion Lemma 10.2 / Prop 10.3 (Type II), Lemma 11.1 (block sieve) and Lemma 11.2 (density), as Inputs 2–4. The arithmetic here (progression twist, Kummer splitting, balanced-pair sieve) is self-contained and correct given those Inputs.
